lines.text: Principal Grayson has not smiled in 22 years.
Teachers have a bet going. The pot is up to $800.
nobody has ever collected.
And right now, you're sitting across his desk.
because you set off the fire alarm by accident while trying to open a window.
He looks at you over his glasses.
He picks up his pen. He says, Do you have anything to say for yourself?
you shrug and say the first thing that comes into your head.
Honestly, sir, the window started it.
He stares at you. His mouth twitches.
Then he makes a sound like a goose being stepped on.
Then, he laughs so hard he slides off his chair and onto the carpet.
His secretary runs in. She hears him laughing, and she starts laughing too.
Ten minutes later, there's no detention.
Twenty minutes later, he's wiping his eyes and asking you to leave.
if you'd like to read the morning announcements.
Every teacher in the building hears him laughing through the wall.
Nobody wins the bet because nobody believes it.
Most people have a sense of humor of about 10.
You have 1000.
It started that morning. You came downstairs and said
Mom, the toast is burnt. That's it.
That's the whole sentence. Your mom laughed so hard she had to sit on the kitchen floor.
Your little brother Noah laughed so hard milk came out of his nose.
Even the dog made a weird happy sound.
Which sounds crazy, but animals laugh too.
Scientists found that rats make tiny chirping sounds when they're tickled.
They're too high for humans to hear, but they're laughing.
At first, it's the best thing that's ever happened to you.
In history class, the teacher asks when the Second World War ended. You don't know.
You say, before I was born, probably.
the whole class falls apart.
The teacher puts her head on the desk and shakes.
you get extra credit for the answer.
In the cafeteria, you tell your best friend Ben that the meatloaf looks nervous.
The table laughs. Then the next table.
then the whole room.
Laughter is contagious, and that's real.
Scientists found that just hearing someone laugh...
switches on the parts of your brain that get you ready to laugh too.
Within a minute, 300 kids are laughing.
and most of them never even heard what you said.
The lunch lady laughs so hard she gives everyone free dessert.
and Ava. Ava sits two rows in front of you in science.
She has never once noticed you exist.
On Wednesday, she drops her pencil.
You pick it up and say, I think it was trying to escape.
She laughs. Not a polite laugh. A real one.
Then she turns around and looks at you.
Like she's seeing you for the first time.
Here's the strange thing about laughing.
Most of it has nothing to do with jokes.
One researcher spent years secretly listening to people laugh in malls, parks, and offices.
He found that most laughs came after totally normal sentences.
Like, I'll see you later. Or, are you sure?
And people are about 30 times more likely to laugh when they're with someone than when they're alone.
Laughing isn't really about funny.
It's how people say, I like you. I'm safe with you.
So with you, everyone feels safe all the time.
On Saturday, a police officer pulls your mom over for speeding.
She's gripping the wheel, terrified.
You lean over from the passenger seat and say, In our defense, officer, the road was very long.
The officer laughs so hard he has to lean on the car.
He doesn't give her a ticket. He gives her directions to a better pizza place.
Mom drives the rest of the way home at exactly the speed limit, staring at you like you're a magic trick.
Then it gets bigger. The School Talent Show.
You don't even prepare.
You walk on stage, look at the audience, and say, wow, there's a lot of you.
The gym explodes. Someone films it.
By Monday, it has 40 million views.
A comedy club in the city invites you to perform. You're 15. They let you in through the back door.
You tell one story about your grandpa's hearing aid.
and a man in the front row laughs so hard he has to leave in an ambulance. He's fine.
He sends you a fruit basket.
Then, a late night TV show calls, live, in front of the whole country.
You sit on the couch next to the host.
he asks how school is going. You say, it's going mostly in the wrong direction.
The audience laughs for 40 minutes.
The show runs out of time. The news after it starts late.
people across the country are laughing in their living rooms.
at a joke they've already forgotten.
That might sound impossible, but something like it actually happened.
In 1962, in a girls school in what is now Tanzania,
a few students started laughing and couldn't stop.
It's spread to other students, then to their families.
Then to nearby villages, about a thousand people were affected.
Schools had to close for months.
Laughter can travel like a cold.
and then you find out what your humor can really do.
Your grandpa hasn't laughed in two years.
not since grandma died. He sits in his chair by the window.
And when you visit, he says...
Hey kid, and that's about it.
On Sunday, you sit down next to him.
and tell them about the man in the ambulance and the fruit basket.
And Grandpa laughs. He laughs until he's crying.
And then he's just crying.
And then he's laughing again. When you leave, he's standing at the door.
He hasn't walked you to the door in two years.
So, you start visiting the children's hospital, every Saturday.
You go room to room. Kids with broken legs.
Kids after surgery, kids who've been there for months.
You make them laugh. A nurse tells you something you didn't know.
When people laugh together, their bodies release chemicals that can make pain easier to handle.
Scientists tested it. People who'd just been laughing in a group.
could hold their hands in ice water.
longer than people who hadn't. The kids on your floor.
ask for less pain medicine on Saturdays. For a while...
You think you're the luckiest person alive.
Then comes the cost. It starts small. You fail a math test.
A real F. You walk into the kitchen and tell your mom.
Mom, I failed math.
She laughs. She can't stop.
She says, Oh honey, you're so funny.
She's not being mean, she just can't hear it any other way.
You get into a fight with Ben. A real one.
He wanted to come to the TV show
and you forgot to ask the producers. You knock on his door to apologize.
You say, Ben, I'm really sorry. I messed up.
Ben starts laughing. He laughs and he's angry at the same time.
and he closes the door in your face.
laughing. You walk Ava home after school.
You've practiced the words for a week.
At her gate, you say.
Ava, I really like you.
She laughs so hard she has to hold on to the fence
You're hilarious, she says.
and she goes inside. That night, you stand in front of the bathroom mirror.
You look at yourself and say,
very quietly, I'm not okay.
And you laugh. Even you can't take you serious.
So, you stop talking.
You don't answer questions in class.
You don't tell stories at dinner.
You point at things in the cafeteria.
You write notes, but the notes are funny too.
Somehow, every word that comes out of you.
in any form, lands like a punchline.
Kids start saying you've become mysterious. They think it's a bit. They laugh at that too.
The only person who notices is Ben.
Three weeks later, he finds you sitting alone on the bleachers.
He sits down a few seats away. He doesn't say anything for a long time.
Then he says, you haven't talked in three weeks. You nod.
He says, is it bad? You nod again.
and Ben for the first time since this started.
Doesn't laugh. He just stays.
Friday, the end of year assembly.
800 students packed into the gym.
Principal Grayson is on stage telling jokes now.
terrible ones every morning. You're sitting near the back.
by the door to the hallway behind the stage, and you smell it first.
smoke, thin gray.
Coming from under the door, something in the old boiler room is burning.
and the fire alarm hasn't gone off. Later, the
The fire department will say the smoke detector in that hallway had a dead battery. You stand up.
you walk to the front. You take the microphone from Principal Grayson.
and you say it as clearly as you can.
Everyone, there's a fire.
We need to leave. Now!
800 people laugh.
It's the biggest laugh you've ever gotten.
Teachers are wiping their eyes. Principal Grayson is bent over.
slapping his knee. Nobody moves.
Behind the stage, the smoke is getting thicker. You can see it now.
curling under the curtain. You try again.
I'm serious, please!
They laugh harder.
You look for help and there's exactly one face in the whole gym that
isn't laughing. Ben.
He's already standing. He's already looking at the curtain.
He believes you. So you stop trying to be serious.
If they're going to laugh, let them laugh all the way out the door.
You lift the microphone. Okay.
Everybody who's ever pretended to understand a math problem, stand up.
The whole gym stands up, howling. Great! Now follow me!
because I'm about to show you the most beautiful thing in this building, the exit.
You start walking toward the doors.
waving your arms like a tour guide.
Ben grabs the shoulders of the kid.
in front of him and starts a conga line.
than everyone does.
800 kids and 40 teachers laughing.
doing a conga line out the gym doors, down the hall.
across the parking lot all the way onto the football field. You keep talking the whole time.
You don't even know what you're saying.
They just keep following the sound.
The last person out is Principal Grayson, still laughing.
holding the microphone stand like a dance partner.
Ninety seconds later, the hallway behind the stage fills with smoke.
Then the fire alarm finally goes off. Then the sirens.
800 people stand on the football field.
and watch the fire trucks pull up. And slowly...
One by one, they stop laughing.
They look at the smoke pouring out of the gym roof.
Then they look at you. The fire chief walks over with a clipboard.
Fastest evacuation I've ever seen, he says.
Can I ask why everyone was laughing?
Ben answers for you. He told them the truth, they just didn't believe it.
On Monday, the whole school makes a rule.
Principal Grayson announces it himself.
Nobody laughs. If you raise your hand, it means you're serious.
And when you raise your hand, people listen.
You raise your hand in the kitchen and tell your mom about the math test.
She doesn't laugh. She helps you study.
You raise your hand on Ben's doorstep and say sorry.
He says, took you long enough and lets you in.
you raise your hand at Ava's Gate.
I really like you. She looks at your hand. She looks at you. She doesn't laugh.
She smiles. I know, she says.
I just wanted you to say it seriously.
Your humor is still a thousand.
You still can't order a pizza without the delivery guy wheezing on the phone.
But now, there's a way to be heard. On Sunday, you visit Grandpa. He's got...
something for you. He's been practicing all week. He clears his throat.
Why don't skeletons fight each other? You wait. They don't have the guts.
It's a terrible joke. It's the worst joke you've ever heard and you laugh
so hard you fall off the couch because for
For the first time in months, someone
made you laugh instead of the other way around.
So, would you want a sense of humor of 1000? If you say yes, prove it.
Tell us the worst joke you know.
in the comments. And if you'd have started that conga line too, hit like and subscribe.
